title: Medicare Costs for Military Retirees in 2027

sections.content: If you are a military retiree with Medicare and TRICARE For Life (TFL), the main 2027 budget change is your Medicare Part B premium. TFL helps with eligible medical bills, but you remain responsible for your Part B premium.

CMS released the following amounts on November 17, 2026, effective January 1, 2027. These are confirmed figures, not estimates. [Source: CMS 2027 premiums and deductibles](https://www.cms.gov/newsroom/fact-sheets/2027-medicare-parts-b-premiums-deductibles).

items: Standard Part B premium: $209.40 per month, compared with $202.90 in 2026, an increase of $6.50.
Part B annual deductible: $292, compared with $283 in 2026, an increase of $9.
Part A inpatient hospital deductible: $1,776 per benefit period, compared with $1,736 in 2026, an increase of $40.
Part A hospital coinsurance for days 61 through 90: $444 per day, compared with $434 in 2026, an increase of $10.

sections.content: The Part A hospital deductible applies per benefit period, rather than once a calendar year. These Medicare cost-sharing amounts are not necessarily bills you will pay yourself when TFL also covers the service.

sections.text: How Much More Will You Pay for Part B?

sections.content: For one person paying the standard premium for all 12 months, the calculation is $202.90 × 12 = $2,434.80 in 2026 and $209.40 × 12 = $2,512.80 in 2027. That is $78 more per year. For a couple with both spouses paying the standard premium all year, the increase is $156.

This example excludes income-related surcharges and late enrollment penalties. Do not automatically add the $9 deductible increase to your household spending: TFL generally covers Medicare cost-sharing when both programs cover the care.

sections.text: How TRICARE For Life Works With Medicare

sections.content: [TRICARE's coverage rules](https://tricare.mil/Plans/HealthPlans/TFL) explain that TFL is automatic for TRICARE-eligible people with Medicare Parts A and B. There is no TFL enrollment fee. You must keep Part B and pay its premium to maintain TFL, including while living overseas.
For covered civilian care in the United States, Medicare generally pays first and TFL follows. Other insurance can change payment order. What you owe depends on which program covers the service:

items: Both programs cover it: generally no out-of-pocket medical cost-sharing.
Medicare covers it, but TRICARE does not: you pay Medicare deductibles and coinsurance.
TRICARE covers it, but Medicare does not: you pay the applicable TRICARE deductible and cost-share.
Neither covers it: you pay the billed charges.

sections.content: TFL can cover services Medicare excludes. Overseas, where Medicare generally does not cover care, TRICARE is usually the primary payer and TRICARE deductibles and cost-shares apply.

sections.text: IRMAA: Which Tax Return Affects Your 2027 Premium?

sections.content: For 2027, Social Security generally uses your 2025 federal income tax return to determine the income-related monthly adjustment amount (IRMAA). If that return is unavailable, SSA may initially use 2024 information and correct the determination when newer data becomes available. This follows SSA's [two-year lookback rule](https://www.ssa.gov/OP_Home/handbook/handbook.25/handbook-2504.html).

Your modified adjusted gross income (MAGI) is adjusted gross income plus tax-exempt interest. Under CMS's 2027 schedule, IRMAA begins above $112,000 for individual filers or $224,000 for joint filers. Special rules apply to married people filing separately who lived together during the tax year. Check the CMS table for your filing status and bracket.
Part B IRMAA still applies when you have TFL. Part D IRMAA applies if you have Medicare prescription drug coverage, not simply because you use the TRICARE pharmacy benefit.

If retirement, reduced work, or another qualifying life-changing event lowered your income, ask SSA whether you can request a lower IRMAA using [Form SSA-44](https://www.ssa.gov/medicare/lower-irmaa). A lower current income does not automatically change the amount on your notice.

sections.text: How Social Security's COLA Fits Into Your Budget

sections.content: SSA has confirmed a [3.6% Social Security cost-of-living adjustment for 2027](https://www.ssa.gov/cola/). If your Part B premium comes out of your Social Security payment, compare your individual benefit increase with your premium change. The dollar increase varies with your benefit amount; it is not the same for every retiree.

The [Part B hold-harmless provision](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-11-19/pdf/2026-23601.pdf) can limit a premium increase that would otherwise reduce an eligible person's net Social Security payment. It has specific benefit and premium-withholding requirements and does not apply to people paying IRMAA. It does not freeze everyone's premium or protect military retired pay.

A premium update does not confirm whether a particular doctor or prescription is covered. Check the provider's Medicare participation and confirm any TRICARE authorization requirements before treatment.

[TRICARE pharmacy coverage is creditable prescription drug coverage](https://newsroom.tricare.mil/News/TRICARE-News/Article/3472382/understanding-medicare-part-d-and-tricare-pharmacy-coverage), so Part D is not required to keep TFL. This drug coverage rule does not give retired beneficiaries permission to delay Part B while keeping TFL. Before adding Part D, compare your medications, costs, and coordination rules.

Use the TRICARE formulary and Express Scripts for your current prescriptions. Medicare Plan Finder compares Part D plans; it does not show your TRICARE pharmacy benefit. This article does not estimate 2027 TRICARE pharmacy copays or your personal treatment costs.

items: Read your 2027 Social Security notice or Medicare bill and confirm your actual Part B premium.
If IRMAA applies, check the tax year, income, filing status, and appeal instructions on your notice.
Keep Part B active and budget for your premium change.
Confirm coverage with TFL and your provider before services that may be covered by only one program.
Check each medication through the TRICARE formulary and contact Express Scripts about coverage or copay questions.

faqs.question: Does TRICARE For Life pay the Medicare Part B premium?
faqs.answer: No. You remain responsible for Part B premiums, including any applicable IRMAA. TFL has no separate enrollment fee.

faqs.question: Will I personally pay the higher Medicare deductibles in 2027?
faqs.answer: Generally, TFL covers Medicare deductibles and coinsurance for services covered by both programs. Different rules apply when only one program covers the service.

faqs.question: Can TFL cover care that Medicare does not?
faqs.answer: Yes. If TRICARE covers the service, its deductible and cost-share may apply even when Medicare pays nothing.

faqs.question: Do military retirees need Part D to keep TFL?
faqs.answer: No. TFL requires Medicare Parts A and B. TRICARE provides creditable prescription drug coverage; review your specific drug needs before adding Part D.

sections.content: For a claim or eligibility question, contact the TFL contractor. For a premium or IRMAA question, contact Social Security. You can review these costs without changing your coverage.

seoTitle: Medicare Costs for Military Retirees in 2027
seoDescription: Review confirmed 2027 Medicare costs for military retirees, the $78 annual Part B increase, IRMAA tax rules, and TRICARE For Life coverage.
excerpt: The confirmed 2027 Medicare costs for military retirees, with a corrected annual Part B example and TRICARE For Life coverage guidance.
keyTakeaways: CMS has confirmed the 2027 Medicare premiums and deductibles.
The standard Part B premium increase adds $78 per person over 12 months.
TFL generally covers Medicare cost-sharing for services both programs cover, but not your Part B premium.
TFL can cover some care Medicare excludes, subject to TRICARE rules.
2027 IRMAA generally uses your 2025 tax return; Part D is not required to keep TFL.
